A free, open-source IPTV player for Android TV, Fire TV and phones. It\'s only a player. It doesn\'t supply channels: you connect the service you already pay for. Nothing you enter leaves your device except to talk to your own provider.

Settee is developed openly, with AI doing a large share of the coding under human direction. That\'s stated plainly, not hidden. Because it\'s open source, no single person going away can take it down: anyone can read every line, build it, and carry it on.
Young Serif and Alegreya Sans, under the SIL Open Font License
Settee plays the TV you already pay for. It doesn\'t supply channels, so start by adding your provider.
Scan a code, then type your details on your phone. Much easier than the remote.
A server address, username and password from your provider.
A link to a playlist, usually ending in .m3u or .m3u8.
A portal address, and the MAC address your provider tied to your line.
For example http://example.com:8080. You can paste the whole line from your provider, and the extra bits get trimmed.
If your provider gave you one long link rather than a login, add it as a playlist instead.
The full http link to your .m3u or .m3u8 file.
The portal address from your provider, such as http://host:port/c/. Extra bits get trimmed.
The MAC your provider tied to your line, e.g. 00:1A:79:xx:xx:xx.
Leave blank to use your provider\'s guide automatically.
Some providers block unfamiliar apps with a 403. If every channel fails, try a common player\'s User-Agent here.
Your provider details stay on this device. Settee has no accounts and no server of its own.
